extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys) handling ex parte appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and required content for an Examiner’s Answer in an ex parte appeal, including identification, approval, explanation, and procedural consequences of new grounds of rejection and related examiner-answer sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs and headings
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must use the prescribed form paragraphs and headings (e.g., form paragraph 12.154.04 for NEW GROUNDS OF REJECTION; 12.179.01 to conclude an answer that raises new grounds; 12.154.05 for WITHDRAWN REJECTIONS; form paragraphs for status of claims, claims appendix, evidence listing, related proceedings, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the MPEP-specified form paragraphs in the indicated sections of the answer; insert the required bracketed content (e.g., dates, claim numbers, signatures) per the Examiner Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent identification of new ground(s) of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new ground(s) of rejection in the examiner’s answer must be prominently identified in both the “Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal” section (form paragraph 12.154) and the “Grounds of Rejection” section (form paragraph 12.159).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 12.154.04 to provide a prominent heading and place the new ground(s) in the specified sections so appellant can readily identify them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory / Technology Center approval for new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new ground of rejection made by an examiner in an answer must be approved by a Technology Center (TC) Director or designee (and if prosecution is reopened after appeal, supervisory approval is required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the personal approval/signature of the TC Director or designee (or SPE when reopening prosecution) in the answer; use form paragraph 12.179.01 to include required approval when new grounds are raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-month reply period and notification of options
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer that contains a new ground of rejection must provide the appellant a TWO MONTHS period to reply and notify the appellant of two options: (1) reopen prosecution by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 (with or without amendment/evidence) or (2) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 that addresses each new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify the appellant of the deadline and the two options (use form paragraph 12.179.01). Explain that extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) do not apply to the TWO MONTH time period but 1.136(b) (patent applications) or 1.550(c) (ex parte reexamination) may apply per 37 CFR 41.39(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when adding new prior art in the answer
rubrics_metrics.description: A new prior art reference applied or cited for the first time in an examiner’s answer generally will constitute a new ground of rejection and must be included in the statement of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a newly cited reference is necessary to support a rejection, positively include it in the statement of rejection. If the reference is cited merely to support an assertion of what is 'well-known' that was first challenged in the appeal brief, it ordinarily will not constitute a new ground (see MPEP § 2144.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: When a change in rationale is not a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: A change in discussion or rationale that preserves the same statutory basis and the same evidence does not necessarily constitute a new ground of rejection; the basic thrust must remain the same so appellant had a fair opportunity to react.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the In re Kronig standard: if statutory basis and evidence remain the same (even if fewer references are relied upon), it may not be a new ground; evaluate whether appellant was given a fair opportunity to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new grounds for previously allowed/objected claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A new ground of rejection would not be permitted to reject a previously allowed or objected-to claim even if the new ground would rely upon evidence already of record; the correct procedure is to reopen prosecution instead of making a new ground in the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If basis for new ground was approved by a supervisor as set forth in MPEP § 1207.04, reopen prosecution rather than adding a new ground in the examiner’s answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examiner’s answer cannot introduce new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental examiner’s answer responding to a reply brief may not include a new ground of rejection (except when written in response to a remand under 37 CFR 41.50(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a supplemental answer responds to issues raised in the reply brief, any additional rejections must not be characterized as new grounds; see MPEP § 1207.05 and 37 CFR 41.43.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation requirements for 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, the Examiner’s Answer shall explain how the first paragraph is not complied with, including, as appropriate, how the specification and drawings do not (a) describe the subject matter defined by each rejected claim, (b) enable one skilled in the art to make and use the claimed subject matter, and (c) set forth the best mode contemplated by the appellant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide claim-specific explanations tied to the specification/drawings; identify deficiencies in written description, enablement, and best mode as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation requirements for 35 U.S.C. 112 second paragraph rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, the Examiner’s Answer shall explain how the claims do not particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter regarded as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete reasons showing lack of clarity/definiteness in claim language and how it fails the second paragraph requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation requirements for 35 U.S.C. 102 rejections (anticipation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102, the Examiner’s Answer shall explain why the rejected claims are anticipated, pointing out where all of the specific limitations recited in the rejected claims are found in the prior art relied upon in the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to explicit locations in the prior art where each limitation appears; be specific (page/figure/line) rather than conclusory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation requirements for 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections (obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103, the Examiner’s Answer shall state the ground of rejection, point out where each of the specific limitations recited in the rejected claims is found in the prior art relied upon, identify the differences between the rejected claims and the primary reference, and explain why it would have been obvious to modify the primary reference to arrive at the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the combination rationale and motivation to combine; identify claim-to-reference correspondences and differences and explain the reasoning that supports obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-by-feature claim-to-art comparison when correspondence is unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: When there may be questions about how claim limitations correspond to features in the prior art, the examiner should compare at least one rejected claim feature-by-feature with the prior art, aligning the claim language side-by-side with references to specific page/line numbers, drawing reference numbers, and quotations from the prior art as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a side-by-side alignment with citations and quotations to remove ambiguity about how each claim limitation is met by the art (see MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation requirement for other rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection other than those specifically listed (112/102/103), the Examiner’s Answer shall specifically explain the basis for the particular rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on terse or boilerplate language; provide a clear, specific factual and legal basis for the rejection so appellant can respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant’s reply options and constraints when maintaining appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant elects to maintain the appeal, they must file a reply brief that addresses each new ground in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(vii) and other brief requirements; a reply brief may not be accompanied by any amendment, affidavit, or other evidence (or it will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply brief should include identification page, status of claims page(s), grounds of rejection to be reviewed page(s), and argument page(s), each beginning on a separate page; a reply brief may substitute the original brief but must meet all brief requirements in 37 CFR 41.37(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to timely reply to new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to timely file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or a reply brief to an examiner’s answer that contains a new ground of rejection, the appeal will be sua sponte dismissed as to the claims subject to the new ground of rejection, and those claims are to be canceled (if all claims are subject, the entire appeal is dismissed and the application may be abandoned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 12.179.02 to dismiss claims subject to the new ground; if only some claims are subject, cancel those claims and continue the appeal as to remaining claims and notify appellant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution after appeal and required approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may reopen prosecution after an appeal (with supervisory patent examiner approval) to enter a new ground of rejection; the Office action reopening prosecution may be made final if (A) the new ground was necessitated by amendment or (B) based on information presented in an IDS under 37 CFR 1.97(c) where no statement under 1.97(e) was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 12.187 to reopen prosecution (insert brief type/date and SPE signature). After reopening, appellant must either file a reply under 1.111/1.113 or initiate a new appeal; previously paid appeal fees may be applied to a later appeal subject to fee differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural handling of replies that are not fully responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply to a new ground is not fully responsive but is bona fide (e.g., addresses the new ground but is incomplete), the examiner should provide a 30-day or 1-month time period (whichever is longer) for appellant to complete the reply pursuant to 37 CFR 1.135(c); if the reply is not bona fide and the two-month period expired, the examiner must sua sponte dismiss the appeal as to the claims subject to the new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the bona fides of the reply; enter and consider bona fide replies and reopen prosecution; provide appropriate completion time if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence listing format and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: When listing the evidence relied upon in the rejection, provide reference information in a standard format (Number Name Date), and use example formats (e.g., '2,717,847 VERAIN 9-1955') as guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 707.05(e) for additional examples and ensure clear identification of references (include figure/label notes where relevant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Related proceedings identification and appendix inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should identify related appeals, interferences, and judicial proceedings known that may be related or have a bearing on the Board’s decision and include copies of all court and Board decisions in a related proceeding(s) appendix using form paragraphs 12.162 and 12.162.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List related proceedings by application/patent/appeal/interference number and include decision copies in the appendix as directed.
